gloss: early evening, early part of the night

definitions.gloss: early evening, early part of the night
definitions.explanation: The period shortly after sunset when the night has just begun, typically around 7-9 PM.

examples.japanese: まだ{宵|よい}の{口|くち}だ。
{宵|よい}の{口|くち}から{飲|の}み{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: We started drinking from early evening.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}の{宵|よい}の{口|くち}は{涼|すず}しくて{気持|きも}ちがいい。
examples.english: Early summer evenings are cool and pleasant.

notes:
The early part of the evening, roughly 7-9 PM. Suggests the night has just begun and there is plenty of time ahead.

USAGE:
Often used in social contexts — especially drinking — to imply "the night is still young." The phrase まだ{宵|よい}の{口|くち}だ means "it's still early in the evening" (so let's keep going).

FORMS:
{宵|よい} (evening, literary) + の + {口|くち} (opening, beginning). Literally: "the mouth/opening of the evening."

RELATED WORDS:
- {宵|よい}: evening (literary, poetic)
- {夕方|ゆうがた}: early evening (more neutral, around sunset)
- {夜|よる}: night (general term)
- {真夜中|まよなか}: midnight, dead of night
